different_problem_class_finding: Stated plainly per the objective: there is NO shared task between Orb-v3 and any module in this portfolio. Orb-v3 maps atomic coordinates to energies and forces; no module here consumes atomic coordinates or emits forces/energies -- every module here predicts formulation- or bulk-scale properties from 2D molecular graphs and composition. An Amphora-vs-Orb comparison is therefore not a benchmark, it is a category error. Matbench Discovery, the field's standard MLIP benchmark (which Orb-v3's own paper and README report against), scores crystal-structure STABILITY prediction -- not Tg, density, refractive index, chi, viscosity, or barrier index -- so a strong Matbench Discovery result says nothing about any quantity this portfolio predicts. The only defensible benchmark is the narrow one this receipt actually answers: MLIP-generated labels vs measured labels for epoxy-amine chemistries, which is a Section C question this portfolio cannot resolve without measured data it does not have.

2_chemistry_coverage.finding: The model the founder actually named -- Orb-v3, arXiv:2504.06231 -- is trained on OMat24 + MPtrj + Alexandria per the paper and orb-models documentation. All three are INORGANIC-CRYSTAL relaxation-trajectory datasets: MPtrj is 'predominantly ... near-equilibrium relaxation trajectories of inorganic bulk materials derived from the Materials Project'; Alexandria is 'theoretical crystal structures in 1D, 2D and 3D ... using DFT'; OMat24 is Meta FAIR's large-scale inorganic-materials AIMD dataset. This confirms the objective's suspicion verbatim: Orb-v3's training distribution is inorganic-crystal-weighted, and epoxy-amine coating chemistry (DGEBA, amine hardeners, organic thermosets) sits OUTSIDE that applicability domain regardless of headline speed or atom-count claims -- the same applicability-domain failure mode this portfolio has already documented for its own models (design-rule-score hull-exit, novelty Mondrian coverage). A coating-relevant DESCENDANT exists -- OrbMol-v2, trained on OMol25 (100M organic+inorganic molecule DFT calcs) plus OPoly26 (6.57M DFT calcs on polymer clusters up to 360 atoms, MD-sampled) -- but OrbMol-v2 is a DIFFERENT, later model, NOT the paper the founder cited (arXiv:2504.06231). No source found in this session states OPoly26 specifically covers amine-cured epoxy thermosets rather than other polymer classes (vinyl, olefin, biopolymer); that specific-class coverage is UNVERIFIED, not assumed from OPoly26's general 'chemical diversity' marketing language.

3_determinism.finding: This is the blocker, and it is now doubly established, not just asserted. (a) Single-inference level: orb-models is a PyTorch-based GNN force field. PyTorch's own official reproducibility documentation (docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.13/notes/randomness.html) states results 'may not be reproducible between CPU and GPU executions, even when using identical seeds', that CUDA atomic operations (e.g. atomicAdd) make floating-point addition order nondeterministic, and that several cuDNN backward routines 'don't guarantee reproducible results even on the same architecture' -- this is a documented, structural property of GPU floating-point reassociation, not an Orb-specific bug, and it applies to any GPU-run MLIP inference. (b) Bulk-property level, which compounds (a): eps_static and density are NOT single-inference MLIP outputs -- Orb/OrbMol supply only energies and forces per configuration. A dielectric constant requires an equilibrated MD trajectory plus a polarization fluctuation-dissipation estimator, and density requires a time-averaged NPT trajectory volume; both add thermostat/barostat integration stochasticity and finite-trajectory statistical noise ON TOP OF the hardware floating-point nondeterminism in (a). VERDICT: MLIP-driven label generation for eps_static/density CANNOT sit inside this portfolio's signed-evidence boundary as it exists today, which requires SHA-256 byte-identical two-replay of the exact computation being signed. OUT-OF-BOUNDARY PATH: generate the label file once, outside the Phase-0 signing boundary (accepting it will not itself be byte-reproducible by the evaluator), then treat the frozen label file as an EXTERNALLY-SOURCED INPUT that enters through the normal evidence-intake-validator path -- exactly the pattern already in production for RadonPy/PI1070 trajectories feeding this module's own existing dielectric KPIs (amphora-molecule-property/reference/mvp20/data/mixed_openpoly_radonpy_dielectric_ml_split_conformal_receipt.v1.json, external_validation_openpoly_dielectric_ml_on_radonpy_pi1070_receipt.v1.json). COST of that path: (i) every label needs its own custody record (exact model checkpoint hash, MD engine + version, seed, hardware, wall clock, thermostat/barostat settings) since the evaluator can never independently re-derive it byte-for-byte; (ii) the Phase-0 two-replay gate can only ever apply to the DETERMINISTIC downstream steps that consume the frozen label file (filtering, admissibility check eps>=n^2, split, fit) -- never to the generation step itself; (iii) the trust chain has a permanent, un-closable gap at generation, identical in shape to the gap this portfolio's own R-D06 ask already names for RadonPy production-convergence confirmation; (iv) the labels remain COMPUTED for the life of the artifact, which matters directly for question 4 below.

4_what_it_cannot_do.finding: Stated plainly, as required: computed labels, however physically admissible by construction, ARE NOT measured labels and CANNOT satisfy any Section C acceptance gate. C.6's acceptance gate explicitly requires 'exact toolkit + identity + mass + rights reconciliation clean' on a rights-clean, >=300-structure corpus, and C.0's common promotion gate requires 'raw evidence complete', 'custody unbroken', and evaluator+reviewer as 'distinct trusted signers' over a 'candidate-bound raw return' from a contract lab -- language that describes wet-lab measurement with custody, not a simulation output file. An MLIP-computed eps_static/density corpus, even a rights-clean, chemistry-appropriate, well-provenanced one, is at best a MODELING PRIOR or a sanity-check bound on the measured campaign, exactly as this portfolio already treats its own physical/group-contribution models -- never a substitute for the candidate-bound wet-lab measurement under two distinct signatures that Phase-1 requires.

objective: FOUNDER QUESTION, SCOPED (directive U-MLIP, section C.6-adjacent). The founder asked whether the system should be benchmarked against Orb-v3 (arXiv:2504.06231, Rhodes et al. 2025), a universal machine-learned interatomic potential (atomic coordinates in, energies/forces out). Starting position, stated up front and not quietly dropped: this is a DIFFERENT PROBLEM CLASS from every module in this portfolio, which predicts formulation- and bulk-scale properties from 2D molecular graphs and composition, not from atomic coordinates, and emits no forces or energies. There is no shared task, so an Amphora-vs-Orb head-to-head benchmark would be a manufactured claim and is explicitly NOT what this item asks for. The real, narrower, answerable question: could an MLIP-driven MD pipeline generate labels that close the C.6 gap -- physically-admissible dielectric labels (currently 89.5% of existing labels are inadmissible, every dielectric model arm scores R^2 <= 0 on the physically-valid subset per docs/directives/2026-08-05-closing-the-open-portfolio.md section C.6) and a second density corpus. Answered via cited primary/secondary source research (WebFetch/WebSearch against arXiv, the orb-models GitHub repo, the OrbMol/OrbMol-v2 Hugging Face model cards, the OMol25/OPoly26 dataset pages, and PyTorch's official reproducibility documentation), not by installing or running anything -- per this item's explicit scope lock (no heavyweight install, no MD run this fire).

why: The compound claim -- 'an MLIP could close the dielectric label gap rights-cleanly' -- fails on multiple independent, cited grounds, any one of which is sufficient to refute it as stated: (1) the specific model the founder named (Orb-v3, arXiv:2504.06231) is trained on inorganic-crystal data (OMat24/MPtrj/Alexandria) and sits outside epoxy-amine coating chemistry's applicability domain by its own documented training distribution -- not an assumption, a citation; (2) even the coating-adjacent descendant model (OrbMol-v2 + OPoly26) cannot be asserted 'rights-clean' because its polymer training data's licence could not be pinned to a verbatim primary-source quote in this session -- the only signal found was arXiv's manuscript-level CC BY 4.0 badge, which this receipt explicitly declines to conflate with a data-file licence; (3) MLIP-driven MD generation of eps_static/density is structurally incompatible with this portfolio's byte-identical two-replay signing boundary -- documented GPU floating-point nondeterminism (PyTorch's own docs) compounded by MD ensemble-sampling stochasticity -- so the computation itself can never be the signed artifact, only a frozen external input with a permanent provenance gap; (4) even a hypothetically rights-clean, chemistry-appropriate, well-provenanced MLIP label corpus would still be COMPUTED, not MEASURED, and Section C's acceptance gate and C.0's promotion gate both require candidate-bound wet-lab measurement with custody and two distinct signatures -- an MLIP corpus cannot satisfy that gate under any of the rights/coverage/determinism outcomes above. 'Could close the gap rights-cleanly' is refuted; the honest scoped answer is that an MLIP-driven pipeline could at best supply an out-of-boundary, chemistry-unverified, rights-partially-unverified MODELING PRIOR that still requires the wet-lab campaign C.6 already specifies.
